target_customer: Independent chefs, bakers and pop-up food sellers in the US who sell by pre-order
problem: Solo food makers need a simple way to announce a sale, take pre-orders and coordinate local pickups without building a store.
business_model: SaaS and payments for chefs (storefront and pre-order tool; fee model not verified)
product_category: Online ordering platform for independent food businesses

technical_complexity.rationale: Storefront, pre-order and pickup scheduling plus payments; standard web commerce.

defensibility.rationale: Chef customer lists and sale workflows add stickiness, but generic storefront and newsletter tools can be adapted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found; general commerce tools (undated sources) could serve the same chefs.

market_need_then: The 2020 pandemic pushed home and pop-up bakers online; Hotplate began as a marketplace and moved to an ordering platform for pop-up chefs (Baking For Business podcast, undated). No hard demand figures found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Chef-friendly and plain ('our why' page, Notion handbook)

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative kitchen word that suits the product, but the name is shared with an unrelated UK business that closed in 2025 and no brand press was found.

pivots.to: Online ordering platform for pop-up chefs and bakers
pivots.why: Not stated beyond the co-founder saying they pivoted away from the marketplace (podcast snippet; date unknown)

outcome_analysis: Hotplate is active with about 9 staff and reports only a roughly $2.85M seed in February 2022 after the S20 batch; no Series A is confirmed. It narrowed from a marketplace to a tool for pre-selling chefs, which appears to have worked well enough to keep operating, but one third-party site's revenue claim ($2.7M in 2024) is unverified. Evidence is too thin to attribute success to specific factors.
notes: Seed: Seedtable and CB Insights agree on date 2022-02 and about $2.85M to $2.9M, both aggregators with no primary filing, so treat the amount as moderately reliable. Investors conflict: Caplight adds Ripple Impact Investments, Roach Capital and Propeller; CB Insights lists only Wave Capital; only Wave Capital and YC recorded. A $150K YC round dated 2020-08 appears in some sources, not recorded. Unverified: $2.7M revenue (2024), one profile. Another profile names Andy Prevalsky as co-founder with founding 2019; YC says 2020. HQ: San Francisco per YC, Austin per another. No competitor with a source dated near 2020 was found, list left empty; The Bake Market and Airmart sources were undated or about supplies. Name origin not found. Not to be confused with a UK business of the same name.
